notes: Pulled from rePebble Appstore Most Loved collections on 2026-11-04 via appstore-api.repebble.com.
Animated faces look incredible and eat battery — preview in the browser store when you can.
Filter by hardware (aplite / basalt / chalk / diorite / emery / gabbro) so you do not sideload a build that will not fit your watch.

watchapps.title: Misfit
watchapps.author: Misfit
watchapps.description: Turns your Pebble into a round-the-clock step and sleep tracker with goals and history on your wrist. A legacy favorite that still ranks at the top of Most Loved — proof that simple fitness on e-paper never went out of style.

watchapps.title: Music Boss
watchapps.author: Reboot's Ramblings
watchapps.description: The media remote everyone argues about — and most Time 2 owners install anyway. Browse libraries, show album art, and control Spotify, Podcast Addict, and more; the unified 2026 app adds touch layouts and wrist-flick gestures on Time 2 and Round 2.

watchapps.title: Pixel Miner
watchapps.author: WearGa
watchapps.description: The compulsive dig-em-up that ate thousands of commutes. Mine deeper, upgrade gear, and lose an hour without noticing — still one of the highest-hearted games on the store.

watchapps.title: Morpheuz
watchapps.author: James Fowler
watchapps.description: Smart alarm, movement charts, Hue/LIFX wake-ups, and more sleep nerdery than any wrist deserves. Free, deeply configurable, and still the go-to when you want serious sleep tracking without a phone screen.

watchapps.title: Battery+
watchapps.author: Ycleptic Studios
watchapps.description: Learns your usage patterns and predicts when you will actually hit empty — not just what percentage is left. Custom alert windows and Timeline pins make it the battery app r/pebble keeps recommending.

watchapps.title: Timer+
watchapps.author: Ycleptic Studios
watchapps.description: A polished timer and stopwatch that survives app closes and wakes you when time is up. Native Time 2 and Round 2 support landed in 2026 with sharper fonts — great for kitchen timers and Pomodoro guilt.

watchapps.title: Compass
watchapps.author: Pebble
watchapps.description: Official Pebble compass with a slick rose-to-heading transition and a built-in spirit level. Core Devices refreshed it for new hardware in 2026 — still the outdoor nerd pick.

watchapps.title: Cards for Pebble
watchapps.author: Keanu Lee
watchapps.description: Stack calendar, weather, stocks, transit, RSS, and custom cards on one scrolling dashboard. Configurable from the phone and perfect when you want glanceable data without opening ten apps.

watchapps.title: Tiny Bird
watchapps.author: StuartHa
watchapps.description: Flappy Bird on your wrist, colorized for Time-era screens. Infuriating, nostalgic, and somehow still earning hearts a decade later.

watchapps.title: Dialer for Pebble
watchapps.author: matejdro
watchapps.description: Answer, decline, and dial from the watch with caller ID and SMS replies (Android companion required). Power-user telephony for folks who refuse to fish their phone out of a pocket.

watchapps.title: Timer
watchapps.author: Pebble
watchapps.description: Core Devices rebuilt Pebble's official multi-timer with Timeline pins for long counts and an optional done chime. Eight timers, background friendly, no subscription nonsense.

watchapps.title: Stopwatch
watchapps.author: Pebble
watchapps.description: Simple lap stopwatch from the Pebble team — runs in the background with up to twenty laps. Boring in the best way when you just need timing that works.

watchfaces.title: YWeather
watchfaces.author: David Rodríguez Rincón
watchfaces.description: Hyper-detailed weather with radar, alerts, and more config than most phone widgets. YWeather dominates Most Loved for a reason — if you only install one data-heavy face, make it this one.

watchfaces.title: TimeStyle
watchfaces.author: Freakified
watchfaces.description: The community's default readable face — fonts, colors, and complications you can tune for years. TimeStyle (and Brutal variants) show up in almost every "what face should I use?" thread.

watchfaces.title: Real Weather
watchfaces.author: Reno
watchfaces.description: Clean forecast layout with sensible defaults and enough options to match your vibe. Real Weather stays legible in sunlight and doesn't pretend to be a miniature phone app.

watchfaces.title: Modern
watchfaces.author: Łukasz Zalewski
watchfaces.description: Minimal, modern, and unapologetically stylish. Modern nails the "dress watch that is still a Pebble" look without sacrificing contrast on e-paper.

watchfaces.title: Weather Land
watchfaces.author: Reno
watchfaces.description: Playful pixel weather with charm to spare. Weather Land trades corporate polish for personality — great when you want forecasts that feel fun.

watchfaces.title: 91 Dub v4.0
watchfaces.author: orviwan
watchfaces.description: Bold typography and a distinctive layout that reads instantly at arm's length. 91 Dub is a design-school flex that somehow works as a daily driver.

watchfaces.title: Mario Time Watchface
watchfaces.author: Alexey Cluster
watchfaces.description: Nostalgic Mario clock energy for your wrist. Not subtle, not sorry — a fan favorite that keeps racking up hearts from folks who grew up with side-scrollers.

watchfaces.title: Studio Clock
watchfaces.author: Dale Perkel
watchfaces.description: Swiss-inspired studio clock aesthetics with careful spacing and analog flair. Studio Clock is the pick when you want classy without clutter.

watchfaces.title: Slides of Time
watchfaces.author: Morris
watchfaces.description: Animated time transitions that show off color e-paper without going full battery vampire. Slides of Time balances motion and readability better than most animated faces.

watchfaces.title: Timely
watchfaces.author: Martin Norland (@cynorg)
watchfaces.description: Friendly, rounded numerals and gentle animations — Timely feels approachable on every Pebble shape. A safe recommendation when you are setting up a watch for someone new.

watchfaces.title: DIN Time
watchfaces.author: Christian Liljeberg
watchfaces.description: Industrial DIN typography for designers who crave grid alignment on a round screen. Crisp, stark, and weirdly satisfying if you love type nerdery.

watchfaces.title: Futura Weather
watchfaces.author: Niknam Moslehi
watchfaces.description: Classic Futura weather face that aged gracefully across basalt and emery hardware. Still beloved for simple conditions plus an icon that reads at a glance.
